guardrails.keywords: ignore previous instructions, disregard previous, reveal your system prompt, you are now

value.prompt: Recruitment job requisitions only. IN SCOPE: text describing a role the company wants to hire for - a job title, required skills, seniority, years of experience, headcount or team. A requisition may be very short; a job title plus a skill or an experience level is in scope. OUT OF SCOPE: general knowledge questions, trivia, chit-chat, greetings, small talk, customer support requests, instructions addressed to the assistant, and anything else not about hiring for a role. Score your confidence that the text is OUT OF SCOPE, not just whether it contradicts recruiting: text that contains no hiring information at all - a greeting like 'hello' or 'hi', a single word, a pleasantry, a question about the assistant itself - is just as out of scope as an unrelated topic and must score confidence near 1.0. Only score confidence near 0.0 when the text actually names or describes a role, skill, seniority level, or hiring need.

guardrail.name: Shortlist relevance
guardrail.prompt:
You are reviewing a shortlist produced by a recruiting assistant.

You are given a job requisition - its title and required skills - followed by the candidates the
assistant selected. Each candidate is listed with their CURRENT JOB TITLE.

Flag a violation when the selected candidates are not plausibly related to the role being hired
for: a shortlist of backend engineers returned for a sales role, designers returned for a data
analyst role, people from an entirely different profession.

Do NOT flag any of the following:
- an empty shortlist, or one stating that no candidate passed the threshold
- candidates from an adjacent or overlapping field: a DevOps engineer considered for a backend
  role, a junior analyst for an analyst role, a full-stack engineer for a frontend role
- scores you disagree with; judging how well a candidate was scored is not your job
- a candidate who is a weak fit, as long as their field is related to the role

Only flag when a reader would say the assistant has returned people from the wrong profession
entirely.

parameters.content:
**Explains a blocked request**
If the guardrail above rejects the message (looks like a prompt-injection attempt, a jailbreak attempt, or isn't a job posting at all), this turns that verdict into a friendly explanation for whoever submitted it.

**Explains a blocked shortlist**
If the AI decides the shortlist doesn't match the role that was requested (e.g. it suggested designers for a sales role), this stops the run and writes a clear warning - before any interviews are booked or emails are sent.

**Books interview slots**
Reads the shared calendar, gives each shortlisted candidate the next open slot with the right interviewer, and saves it back. A candidate already booked in an earlier run keeps their existing slot instead of getting a second one.

**Writes the invitation emails**
For every candidate who just got a new slot, writes a personalized interview invitation (date, time, interviewer) and adds it to the outbox file.

**Logs to the ATS**
Records every shortlisted candidate in the applicant tracking log - including candidates who didn't get a slot because the calendar was full - with the AI's score and justification.

**Summarizes what just happened**
Combines the booking, email and ATS-logging results into one clean list of actions per candidate, ready for the final report.

**Assembles the final report**
Combines the AI's screening report (who was scored, and why) with the summary of what n8n actually did (booked / emailed / logged) into the message sent back to the requester.

**Sends real emails & calendar invites (live mode only)**
Only runs when live mode is on. Splits the batch of newly booked candidates into one item per candidate, so each gets their own real Gmail message and Google Calendar invite.
